channel.title: US Top News and Analysis
channel.description: CNBC is the world leader in business news and real-time financial market coverage. Find fast, actionable information.

item.title: Trump waives broad new Russia sanctions and tariffs under Graham Act, citing national interest
item.description: Trump signed the Graham Bill, which targeted Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, into law in September.

item.title: Software’s new consolidator gets big vote of confidence from Berkshire
item.description: Less than four months into life as a public company, Bending Spoons got a big vote of confidence this week from Berkshire Hathaway.

item.title: Berkshire shares buck market sell-off, rally to highest since Buffett said he would step down as CEO
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway shares are at their highest level since Warren Buffett told shareholders at the May 2025 annual meeting he planned to step down as CEO at the end of that year.

item.title: 5 midterm money takeaways: Democrats have candidate cash. Republicans have Elon Musk
item.description: Democrats outraise Republicans in key Congress races as Elon Musk funds Ken Paxton in Texas and GOP groups aligned with Trump.

item.title: 'Dead money’ for a decade: Why this hedge fund approach may deliver an advantage over bonds
item.description: Investors may want to rethink their bond allocation and opt for managed futures exposure.

item.title: These tech stocks are a buy ahead of their earnings reports, Bank of America says
item.description: Bank of America says there are several technology stocks that have more room to run heading into their next quarterly results.

item.title: Semiconductor market to remain solid ‘at least through next year,’ South Korea finance minister says
item.description: South Korea's finance minister said semiconductor growth can last at least through 2027 as supply remains tight despite a global chip sell-off.

item.title: Trump's student loan overhaul could lead to more bankruptcy filings, former judge says
item.description: After nearly three decades as a bankruptcy judge, Sarah Sharer Curley writes about the legal process in her new book, "The Price of Forgiveness."

item.title: Airport attacks put aviation in crosshairs of geopolitical conflicts
item.description: Deadly attacks at Riyadh’s main airport are disrupting airlines, closing airspace and raising new security questions for commercial aviation.

item.title: Investors are buying up vast tracts of timberland across U.S. in one of market's longest-term bets
item.description: Timberland managers buying for pension funds and other institutional investors can wait decades for returns, but the market can also be a profit trap.

item.title: KFC to switch to Coca-Cola beverages in U.S. restaurants for the first time in decades
item.description: KFC is switching from PepsiCo to Coca-Cola as its beverage supplier for U.S. restaurants.

item.title: 'Everyone laughed' when he started a pumpkin farm—now it brings in $2 million a year
item.description: Kelly Schultz bought a pumpkin farm in 1996. He transformed it into a seasonal attraction that draws in 100,000 visitors each fall.

item.title: South Texas Latino voters who flipped for Trump in 2024 are up for grabs in 2026
item.description: Hispanic and Latino voters swung hard for President Donald Trump in 2024. But in the 2026 midterm election, Democrats are pushing to get them back.

item.title: Nasdaq slides 2% Friday to post worst week since June, pressured by AI sell-off and oil prices: Live updates
item.description: Investors shunned the artificial intelligence trade and oil prices spiked on Friday, dragging the three major averages to losses.

item.title: Looking for a non-AI trade? This bank stock is poised for a breakout next week
item.description: For JPMorgan, the upside potential appears greater than the downside risk.

item.title: IMFC chair says global economy resilient; delegates walk out on Russian official
item.description: "Escalating conflicts and trade tensions could further disrupt critical trade routes," the chair of the International Monetary and Financial Committee said.

item.title: U.S. budget deficit swells to almost $2 trillion for fiscal 2026, up 12% in a single year
item.description: The Treasury Department published the U.S. budget deficit for the 2026 fiscal year.

item.title: Hurricane Trudy approaches Mexico coast as Typhoon Champi threatens Guam
item.description: Hurricane Trudy moved toward Mexico's Pacific coast and could keep growing through Saturday, forecasters said.

item.title: Some companies give AI to everyone. This CEO is doing the opposite
item.description: Paysend CEO Ben Chisell limits AI tools to top performers as other U.K. companies push broader workplace rollouts.

item.title: Tesla unveils long-delayed Roadster developed with SpaceX, fueling merger speculation
item.description: Elon Musk first debuted the Roadster refresh concept in 2017 but Tesla has since missed every targeted delivery date.

item.title: AI stocks plunge. Inflation heats up. Where we're still finding opportunities
item.description: The sinking AI trade rattled last week's market. But solid bank earnings and a rotation beyond tech gave us reasons for optimism.

item.title: What happens after bankruptcy? A debt attorney explains what comes next
item.description: Learn what happens after bankruptcy, how it affects your credit, plus steps to rebuild with guidance from a debt attorney.

item.title: Prediction market odds on Tesla-SpaceX merger are above 50% for early 2027
item.description: Kalshi odds for a Tesla-SpaceX merger rose above 50% for early 2027 as Barclays outlined how a deal could work.

item.title: Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo puts the company's status-symbol power to the test
item.description: Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo is drawing early demand as analysts assess whether the foldable can lift iPhone pricing and revenue.

item.title: Katie Zacharia out as Trump's White House press secretary
item.description: Zacharia was on shaky ground from her first White House press conference and over questions about her claims of being a lawyer despite not passing a bar exam.

item.title: Wall Street's fear gauge is ripping. Traders see it going even higher
item.description: The sell-off in AI-related stocks pushed the VIX above 22 for the first time in four months. A cluster of trades suggests it could go even higher.

item.title: Why Trump and the GOP's billion-dollar midterm blitz isn’t working
item.description: Trump-aligned groups and Elon Musk have poured hundreds of millions into the midterm election, but the GOP spending surge has barely moved polls or the map.

item.title: U.S. presses China on Mastercard, Citigroup market access in bilateral Bangkok talks, official says
item.description: The U.S. raised market access issues for Mastercard and Citigroup in China during bilateral meetings in Bangkok this week, a U.S. Treasury official says.

item.title: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
item.description: The protests began last ‌month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where demonstrations over education morphed into anger about inequality.

item.title: Trump says White House didn't order Starlink restrictions in Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian officials complained this week that SpaceX had limited internet connectivity without advance notice.
